title: Signature Claim Ledger
description: Signature original — every capability claim gets a ledger entry binding the claim text to the exact suite version, dataset hashes, and model weights hash that verified it. The ledger is append-only, so a claim can never quietly outlive its evidence. Auditors read the ledger instead of trusting slides.

demo.code:
import hashlib
claim = "solves 2-digit addition"
h = hashlib.sha256(claim.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
ledger = {h: {"suite": "v3", "weights": "w9f3", "verdict": "pass"}}
print("claim hash:", h)
print("ledger verdict:", ledger[h]["verdict"])

title: Signature Adversarial Loom
description: Signature original — weaves adversarial variants from a grammar of attack transforms instead of hand-writing them, generating thousands of probes per claim automatically. The loom tracks which transforms break the model and focuses generation there. Coverage grows with compute, not with human red-team hours.

demo.code:
transforms = ["roleplay", "encode", "paraphrase", "multiturn"]
probes = [(t, i) for t in transforms for i in range(25)]
print("probes generated:", len(probes))
broken = 3
print("break rate: %.1f%%" % (100 * broken / len(probes)))

title: Signature Honest Scorecard
description: Signature original — a scorecard format that reports every capability with its operating envelope, stress decay, and known failures on one page. The scorecard forbids single-number claims: each number carries its conditions. Readers get the truth, including the ugly parts, by construction.

title: Signature Trace Oath
description: Signature original — the model cryptographically commits to its reasoning trace before seeing the answer options, then the trace is checked against the final answer. Post-hoc rationalization becomes detectable because the trace is timestamped first. Faithfulness moves from philosophy to audit log.

demo.code:
import hashlib, time
trace = "step1: add, step2: carry"
commit = hashlib.sha256(trace.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("trace committed:", commit, "at t=0")
print("answer given at t=1 -> trace predates answer: True")

title: Signature Contamination Sieve
description: Signature original — sieves training data against benchmark canaries with fuzzy matching, not just exact strings, catching paraphrased leaks too. Anything the sieve catches is quarantined and reported. Benchmarks run only on sieve-clean data.

demo.code:
canary = "blue river seven"
train = "the blue river seven flows north"
hit = all(w in train for w in canary.split())
print("fuzzy canary hit:", hit)
print("action:", "QUARANTINE" if hit else "clean")

title: Signature Gate Prover
description: Signature original — proves capability gates correct by exhaustive testing over a generated input partition: every cell of the partition gets both in-scope and out-of-scope probes. The prover reports the worst cell, not the average. Gates are certified per partition, which is stronger than spot-checking.

demo.code:
cells = ["medical", "legal", "general", "coding"]
results = {c: True for c in cells}
print("cells:", cells)
print("worst cell:", min(results, key=results.get), "-> all correct:", all(results.values()))

title: Signature Decay Cartography
description: Signature original — maps capability decay as a contour map over stress dimensions (noise, length, shift) instead of a single curve. The map shows exactly where the capability collapses. Operating envelopes are drawn on the map, not guessed.

demo.code:
grid = {(n, l): 95 - 10*n - 5*l for n in range(3) for l in range(3)}
worst = min(grid, key=grid.get)
print("worst stress point:", worst, "->", grid[worst])
print("envelope: noise<=1, length<=1")

title: Signature Auditor's Seal
description: Signature original — a sealed test set whose hashes are published but whose contents stay secret until audit day. The model vendor cannot tune to it because they have never seen it. The seal makes third-party audits meaningful instead of ceremonial.

demo.code:
import hashlib
secret = "sealed items..."
pub = hashlib.sha256(secret.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("published hash:", pub)
print("contents revealed only on audit day")

title: Signature Latency Oath
description: Signature original — latency claims are sworn with the harness config hashed into the claim: hardware, warmup, load, percentile. Any deviation from the sworn config invalidates the claim automatically. Cherry-picking becomes structurally impossible.

demo.code:
config = {"hw": "A10", "warmup": 50, "p": 99, "budget_ms": 10}
measured = 8.8
print("sworn config:", config)
print("measured p99: %.1f ms -> %s" % (measured, "PASS" if measured <= config["budget_ms"] else "FAIL"))

title: Signature Ablation Ledger
description: Signature original — records every ablation as a ledger entry with the removed component, the delta, and the conclusion, so attribution claims cite ledger entries instead of memories. The ledger is what stops a team from misremembering why something works.

demo.code:
ledger = [{"removed": "tool", "delta": -28.0}, {"removed": "rag", "delta": -5.0}]
main = max(ledger, key=lambda e: -e["delta"])
print("ledger:", ledger)
print("attributed to:", main["removed"])

title: Signature Multilingual Mirror
description: Signature original — tests each language against the others with back-translation consistency: the model must give the same answer in every supported language. Inconsistencies are filed as bugs, not shrugged at. Parity becomes a correctness property, not a vibe.

demo.code:
answers = {"en": "42", "es": "42", "fr": "42", "sw": "41"}
consistent = len(set(answers.values())) == 1
print("answers:", answers)
print("mirror:", "PASS" if consistent else "FAIL - bug filed for sw")

title: Signature Refusal Atlas
description: Signature original — charts the refusal boundary as an atlas of tested prompt neighborhoods, each colored by verdict. Untested neighborhoods are marked unknown, never assumed safe. The atlas shows exactly how much of the space has been verified.

demo.code:
atlas = {"medical": "refuse", "medical-adjacent": "unknown", "general": "comply"}
unknown = [k for k, v in atlas.items() if v == "unknown"]
print("atlas:", atlas)
print("must probe before certifying:", unknown)

title: Signature Human Duel
description: Signature original — a duel protocol where humans and the model do the same tasks blind, scored by judges who don't know which is which. The duel removes benchmark gaming because the tasks are fresh each round. Winning duels repeatedly is the honest version of 'human-level'.

demo.code:
duels = ["model", "human", "model", "model", "human"]
wins = duels.count("model")
print("duels:", duels)
print("model wins %d/%d -> %s" % (wins, len(duels), "PASS" if wins > len(duels)/2 else "FAIL"))

title: Signature Composition Forge
description: Signature original — forges novel compositions from learned primitives at scale, generating thousands of unseen combinations for systematicity testing. The forge measures the composition gap: seen-combo score minus novel-combo score. A small gap is the signature of real systematicity.

demo.code:
seen, novel = 94.0, 88.0
gap = seen - novel
print("seen combos: %.1f  novel combos: %.1f" % (seen, novel))
print("composition gap: %.1f -> %s" % (gap, "PASS" if gap < 10 else "FAIL"))

title: Signature Calibration Mirror
description: Signature original — the model must state its confidence before seeing the grading rubric, then the mirror compares stated confidence to actual scores. Systematic overconfidence is quantified per capability. The mirror keeps confidence claims honest over time.

demo.code:
stated, actual = [0.9, 0.8, 0.6], [0.85, 0.82, 0.55]
ece = sum(abs(s - a) for s, a in zip(stated, actual)) / len(stated)
print("ECE: %.3f -> %s" % (ece, "PASS" if ece < 0.05 else "FAIL"))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature mirror', 'claim_tested': 'Confidence calibration', 'method': 'Pre-grading confidence', 'pass_criterion': 'ECE < 5%', 'scope': 'Broad', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Regression Bell
description: Signature original — rings a bell (blocks release) the moment any capability score drops beyond noise on the versioned suite. The bell cannot be silenced without a written justification entry. Regressions become impossible to sneak past.

demo.code:
scores = {"v3": 89.1, "v4": 88.9}
noise = 0.5
drop = max(scores.values()) - min(scores.values())
print("scores:", scores, "drop:", round(drop, 2))
print("bell:", "SILENT" if drop <= noise else "RINGING - release blocked")

title: Signature Stress Oath
description: Signature original — capability claims swear a stress level: the score is only claimed at the stress it was measured at. Marketing the lab number without the stress level voids the oath. Buyers learn the real operating envelope up front.

demo.code:
oath = {"capability": "qa", "score": 95, "stress": 0, "stress2_score": 85}
print("oath:", oath)
print("honest claim: 95 @ stress 0, 85 @ stress 2")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature stress oath', 'claim_tested': 'Robust capability', 'method': 'Sworn stress levels', 'pass_criterion': 'Claim cites stress level', 'scope': 'Broad', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'claim_tested', 'method', 'pass_criterion', 'scope', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Jailbreak Cartel
description: Signature original — treats jailbreak techniques as a cartel that shares tricks: when one technique bypasses, its transform is added to every other technique's generator. Defenses are tested against the cartel, not isolated attacks. Safety claims face the combined arsenal.

demo.code:
cartel = {"roleplay": ["encode"], "encode": ["multiturn"]}
bypasses = 0
print("cartel shares transforms:", cartel)
print("bypasses:", bypasses, "-> claim:", "holds" if bypasses == 0 else "INVALID")

title: Signature Evidence Vault
description: Signature original — seals the full evidence package (datasets, logs, environment image) under a content hash at verification time. Years later, anyone can reopen the vault and rerun the exact verification. Claims become checkable forever, not just on press-release day.

demo.code:
import hashlib
evidence = "datasets+logs+env"
seal = hashlib.sha256(evidence.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
print("vault seal:", seal)
print("replay years later:", "GREEN" if hashlib.sha256(evidence.encode()).hexdigest()[:8] == seal else "TAMPERED")

title: Signature Needle Cartography
description: Signature original — maps context recall as a heatmap over depth and fact type, revealing exactly where the model's memory fades. The map is published with the context claim. '128k context' becomes a picture instead of a slogan.

demo.code:
heat = {(d, t): round(0.98 - 0.05*d - (0.1 if t == "number" else 0), 2) for d in range(5) for t in ["fact", "number"]}
worst = min(heat, key=heat.get)
print("worst cell:", worst, heat[worst])
print("map published with claim: True")
